clue.text: I rule as hooker's heel stuffs fly half

indicators.note: one piece stuffs another, so it is packed inside it

parts.note: the tsetse is an African fly, and half its name is its first three letters
qua is Latin for 'in the capacity of', i.e. as

indicators.note: a heel is the back end of a foot, so the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A rugby fly half boasts that a hooker's back foot keeps him in line.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby words (hooker, fly half) are misdirection. The definition speaks for the drawing tool itself, which is used to rule lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A draughtsman's T-square is a ruler, so the instrument could say of itself that it rules.

clue.text: City as wild as Jones

indicators.note: wild signals letters going out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: A place as untamed as someone called Jones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges AS JONES.
explanation.definitionFit: San Jose is a city in California and also the capital of Costa Rica.

clue.text: War vessel forbidden to come up to receive oxygen

indicators.note: a vessel that receives something takes it aboard, so here the turned-round word holds the gas inside it
in a down clue coming up reverses the word

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, meaning forbidden
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A warship is barred from surfacing to take in air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come up' turns TABU round to UBAT in this down clue; 'to receive' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat was a German submarine of the World Wars, a vessel of war.

clue.text: Fortify a lamb chop?

definitions.meaning: to fortify a place is to defend it with an earth bank or wall
a chop is a portion cut from a sheep, playfully a part of a ram

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether to strengthen a lamb chop.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to fortify with a defensive wall, and split up it reads as a piece of a male sheep.

clue.text: Benedict ordering pint of Fosters to begin with

indicators.note: putting things in a new order signals that the letters are rearranged
what comes to begin with is the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Pope Benedict asks a barman for a pint of Foster's lager first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' rearranges PINTOF to PONTIF, and 'to begin with' adds F from Fosters, a brand of Australian lager.
explanation.definitionFit: Benedict XVI was the reigning pope when the puzzle appeared, and a pope is the supreme pontiff.

clue.text: They are known by experts working first and working second

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
I is the Roman numeral one, first
again, on means working

explanation.surface: Experts know them as working first and working second.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'to know your onions' means to be expert in a subject, so experts are those who know these.
explanation.definitionFit: Experts are said to know their onions, an idiom for being well informed.

clue.text: Gay clothes poacher's ill-gotten gains?

definitions.meaning: a poacher's catch is what he gets from his traps

explanation.surface: A poacher spends his loot on bright clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappings are ornamental accessories or finery, and playfully the haul from traps.

clue.text: A hot drink for every ball from Warne

parts.note: flip is an old hot drink of beer or spirits with egg and sugar
per means for each

explanation.surface: Someone offers a hot drink for every ball bowled by Shane Warne.
explanation.walkthrough: Shane Warne was a great Australian leg-spin bowler in cricket; the flipper is one of his deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: The flipper is a leg-spinner's delivery that skids on low, which Warne bowled.

clue.text: Ageist ban might state this message of the day?

definitions.text: Ageist ban might state this message of the day?

parts.words: Ageist ban might state this message of the day?
parts.note: read literally, the New Year phrase would be an ageist order to remove elderly people; at year's end it welcomes change

explanation.surface: A slogan for New Year's Eve, which the puzzle date marks.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a proverbial New Year saying about discarding the past to welcome change.

clue.text: Remarkable turn actor gives on a regular basis

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: A performer regularly delivers an outstanding turn on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Unco is a Scots word meaning strange or remarkable, familiar from crosswords.

clue.text: A moralist executed in the end for backing African country

indicators.note: the A and the headless moralist go in the reversed goal
backing means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

indicators.note: executed means beheaded here, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a Puritan is a strict moralist

explanation.surface: A moral crusader is finally put to death for supporting an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' looks like the definition's verb, but here it means beheaded; 'in the end' reads as 'finally' in the surface, yet 'in' is the container and 'end' means a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mauritania is a country in north-west Africa on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Upon which Cicero would have held forth cirrostratus clouds

definitions.text: Upon which Cicero would have held forth

indicators.note: to cloud is to obscure, so the word cirrostratus hides the answer within it

explanation.surface: Cicero's orations are pictured among high sheet clouds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clouds' looks like a noun naming cirrostratus, but it is a verb meaning hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostra are the speakers' platforms of the Roman Forum, where orators like Cicero made speeches.

clue.text: Legal beagle trapping one in port's air duct?

indicators.note: the lawyer with one inside goes into the wine

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: trapping means holding something inside

parts.note: a legal beagle is a sharp lawyer; the DPP is the Director of Public Prosecutions
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A keen lawyer catches someone inside a port's ventilation shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: The DPP is the Director of Public Prosecutions, England's chief prosecutor, a jokey 'legal beagle'; 'port's' is the fortified wine, not a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe or trachea carries air to the lungs, a duct for air in the body.

clue.text: Stew of one apt to have two veg

indicators.note: a stew mixes ingredients up, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a stew is likely to include two vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have' is only a link; the letters of ONE APT and TWO are rearranged by 'Stew of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A new potato is an early, freshly dug potato, a common vegetable.

clue.text: Carriage return at the end of the sentence?

definitions.text: Carriage return at the end of the sentence?

parts.words: Carriage return at the end of the sentence?
parts.note: a typing term read as a vehicle taking a convict back to jail once a judge has sentenced him

explanation.surface: A typing instruction: hit return after a full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A secure vehicle carries convicted prisoners from court to jail after sentencing.

clue.text: Novice called about lump

indicators.note: about signals the word is turned round

parts.note: called on the phone means rang
L is the learner, a novice, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A beginner phoned about a swelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The novice is put last though it comes first in the clue; L is from the learner plates on British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnarl is a knot or lumpy growth on a tree.

clue.text: Oasis reforming for musicians, or…

indicators.note: re-forming means shaping again, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The band Oasis gets back together for its fans, or something follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforming' hints at the Britpop band's reunion, but it rearranges OASIS. The clue runs on into the next one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossia is a term in printed music, Italian for 'or', marking an alternative passage.

clue.text: Lacking depth, everything's in view

indicators.note: everything goes in the view

parts.note: a show is a display or view
everything means all

explanation.surface: Something shallow has all on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'everything's' reads as 'everything is', with only the ALL contributing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallow means having little depth, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: …on the unnamed eve of Keats poem, who's performing Cats?

indicators.note: unnamed means without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: Keats wrote The Eve of St Agnes, so its eve is St Agnes

indicators.note: performing signals the letters are rearranged into a new show

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Someone asks who is performing in Cats on the eve of a Keats poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unnamed' drops N from STAGNES, leaving STAGES; 'performing' rearranges WHO into HOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats, the Lloyd Webber musical, is an example of a theatrical production, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Even more obscene, shopkeeper declared

indicators.note: declared means spoken out, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a grocer keeps a food shop

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper announces something even more indecent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declared' signals the sound of GROCER.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross can mean obscene or coarse, so grosser is more obscene still.

clue.text: The Law of Carroll's Father?

definitions.meaning: Lewis Carroll's poem 'You Are Old, Father William' makes the father an old William

explanation.surface: A question about the law in Lewis Carroll's family.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Bill is British slang for the police, and Bill shortens William in Carroll's old Father William.

clue.text: Dead queen is rising in colour

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read upwards

parts.note: the saying 'Queen Anne's dead' means stale news, so Anne is the dead queen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dead queen's colour is said to be rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses ANNE plus IS, the whole run, in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is a reddish-brown earth pigment and colour.

clue.text: To change physical state of substance, divide 5, as e, by Pi /2

definitions.text: To change physical state of substance

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: one piece divides another by sitting inside it

parts.note: taken as written
read the slash as 'or', so Pi split in two is P or I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mock scientific instruction about turning a liquid to gas by dividing numbers by pi.
explanation.walkthrough: The maths is nonsense: 'divide' puts PORI between VA and SE, and 'Pi /2' reads as P or I.
explanation.definitionFit: To vaporise is to turn a substance into vapour, changing its physical state.

clue.text: Leg positioned in accordance with the rules on another field

definitions.meaning: in cricket the leg side of the field is also called the ...

definitions.text: in accordance with the rules on another field
definitions.meaning: in football or rugby a player in a legal position is not offside

explanation.surface: A footballer's leg is placed within the rules on another pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both cricket's leg side and the legal position of a player in football.

clue.text: The knockdown of Lot 13 in state capital?

parts.note: an auctioneer's hammer knocks a lot down, making the sale
M is the thirteenth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An auctioneer knocks down lot 13 in a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: This is Salem, Oregon's capital, not the Massachusetts town of the witch trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Salem is the capital city of the US state of Oregon.

clue.text: Test venues PE students infiltrate for training

indicators.note: training puts things through drills, signalling the letters are reworked

parts.note: L is a learner, so students are two Ls, who infiltrate by joining the pool of letters

explanation.surface: Students sneak into exam halls and gyms to practise.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Ls end up apart in the answer, so 'infiltrate' cannot be a simple container: the learners join the letters of VENUES PE, and 'for training' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleven-plus was the British school exam taken at about age eleven to decide grammar school places.

clue.text: Cut inside after short cut

indicators.note: after says the inner piece comes after the trimmed one
short means cut off at the end, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to lop is to cut
inside means in

explanation.surface: A barber's instruction: cut the inside after a quick trim.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut appears twice: the first is the definition, the second is part of the wordplay, the setter's deliberate reuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Loin is a cut of meat from the back of an animal.

clue.text: Central African managed to procure stick

indicators.note: to procure is to get, here to get hold of and contain

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so managed is ran
a wand is a slender stick

explanation.surface: A person from central Africa obtained a walking stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' looks like the main verb of the surface, but it is the outer piece holding the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a country in central Africa, so one of its people is Central African.

clue.text: Marsupial not as wild as flower

indicators.note: not marks the letters of as as missing from the pool
wild signals the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kangaroo is said to be less untamed than a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A and S out of MARSUPIAL ('not as') and 'wild' rearranges MRUPIAL into the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The primula is a genus of flowering plants including primroses and cowslips.
